title: SRE weekly operational check-in — Jan 04 2027
content:
Week snapshot (2027-01-04)

Owners: Asha (oncall lead this week), Leo (infra), Sofia (runtime), Marta (observability)
Drive: shared_drives/engineering/site-reliability-engineering
Status: working notes / handoff doc (publish after follow-ups)

High-level summary
- Three notable disruptions this week that affected customer latency and error budget: a KV-cache eviction storm on Dedicated pools, intermittent DNS flapping in eu-west-1 edge nodes, and an autoscaling feedback loop that briefly overprovisioned GPU instances. No customer-facing data exposure.
- Overall SLOs held within tolerance for the week but p95 token latency drifted above target for a 90-minute window on Tuesday. Error budget usage increased by ~0.8% (preliminary).
- Immediate mitigations applied, follow-up action items assigned. Postmortem for the KV-cache event planned for Jan 10.

Incidents (short bullets)
1) KV-cache eviction storm — Jan 02 02:10–03:05 UTC
   - Impact: Elevated gen latency across Dedicated pools serving medium-length contexts (1k–2k tokens). P95 token latency +45% for impacted shards; error rate increased from 0.2% -> 0.9% on affected routes.
   - Root cause (initial): A recent runtime change (PR 912) changed LRU heuristics; combined with an abnormal burst of prefix variations from a customer test harness led to mass eviction + cache thrash.
   - Mitigation: Rolled back PR 912 on affected fleets, temporarily disabled aggressive prefetching, and fenced a noisy customer test run.
   - Follow-ups: Add unit/integration tests for cache eviction under bursty prefix distributions; add metric alert for cache eviction rate per pool; schedule postmortem (owner: Sofia).

2) eu-west-1 edge DNS flapping — Jan 03 14:40–15:20 UTC
   - Impact: 503s from gateway -> edge (approx 12% of edge requests). Affected hosted-api customers routed through eu-west-1; fallback to regional tier worked for most but some requests hit transient errors.
   - Root cause: DNS provider had short-lived rate-limiting on updates combined with our aggressive fallback TTLs; edge proxies retried aggressively and amplified failures.
   - Mitigation: Bumped local resolver TTLs, added jitter to retries, and raised provider support case.
   - Follow-ups: Re-evaluate resolver TTL strategy for edges, add a synthetic check tracing full gateway->edge->runtime path (owner: Leo).

3) Autoscale feedback loop — Jan 01 21:10–21:35 UTC
   - Impact: Temporary overprovisioning of GPU instances in a Dedicated cluster; cost spike observed on billing metric (billing-alert fired). No customer requests dropped, but increased cost and warnings.
   - Root cause: New autoscale policy with conservative downscale grace + sudden drop in request rate caused controller to keep scaling decisions; combined with a metrics smoothing bug produced repeated upscales.
   - Mitigation: Reverted to previous autoscale policy, fixed smoothing logic in controller (hotfix deployed).
   - Follow-ups: Add chaos test for scale-down behavior; ensure cost-alert thresholds are clearer (owner: Marta).

SLOs and metrics highlights- Availability SLO (global): 99.97% for week (on track)- p95 token latency (global): Target 180ms, observed 195ms during Tuesday window; baseline otherwise ~165ms- Cache eviction rate (important new metric): spike to 15 evictions/sec per-shard during incident (baseline <1)- Error budget burn: +0.8% this week, cumulative for quarter ~2.6%

Runbook and playbook notes- Cache-eviction runbook updated with new triage steps; still TODO: exact metric names and dashboard links.- Edge resolver playbook: add a step to temporarily widen TTLs and turn off aggressive retry for 10m to see if stability returns before rotating provider keys.- Autoscale tuning checklist: add a post-deploy verification for controller smoothing window.

On-call handoff (for next shift / next week)
- Current oncall: Asha (lead) until 2027-01-05 16:00 UTC. Next oncall: Leo.
- Handoff items:
  * KV-cache postmortem coordination (Sofia owner) — review notes and confirm rollback conditions for any re-deploy.
  * Edge synthetic test task (Leo) — get a quick smoke test in place for eu-west-1.
  * Autoscale chaos test (Marta) — schedule in staging next Wed.
  * Update pager rules: add eviction-rate >5/sec for 5m alert (work with Observability team to tune).

Open action items (quick list)
- Sofia: draft postmortem for KV eviction (due Jan 10).
- Leo: synthetic path test for eu-west-1 + update retry/jitter docs (due Jan 07).
- Marta: schedule autoscale chaos experiment in staging and update cost alert thresholds (due Jan 12).
- Asha: consolidate runbook edits and publish final doc (due Jan 09).

Notes to self / loose ideas- Consider a small adaptive LRU window for high-variance customers instead of global heuristic.- Maybe add a per-customer cache quota/guardrail to avoid noisy tenants thrashing shared caches.- Revisit edge resolver provider contract (SLA/rate limits).

Meeting and syncs this week- Mon 09:30 SRE standup — quick triage (attendees: SRE, infra, runtime)- Wed 11:00 Postmortem sync (tentative)- Fri 15:00 Runbook review with Observability

References / links- Linear: RW-INC-1342, RW-INC-1348- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/912- Runbook draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/sre/runbooks/cache-eviction

Quick handoff note (for whoever picks this up next): prioritize the KV-cache postmortem slot — it will determine whether we re-enable the changed LRU heuristics. If in doubt, keep the rollback in place until tests pass.

-- Asha
